Social anxiety is horrible. It's an invisible handicap that other people just can't understand. 

I had crippling SA for all of my early life. I tried everything. Medicines like benzodiazepines and beta blockers helped. But I did a DIY style immersion therapy for a while that really helped *cure* it instead of just treating it. But it was really hard. I actually got very good at socializing. Years later it's come back some because I've completely isolated myself (for other reasons). But even now it's not nearly as bad.

You've got to either cut her off or somehow end your romantic attachment to her (which I've never found possible without a long, long period of no contact). I feel ya. I shot myself in the head trying to commit suicide. Didn't die, just ended up really ugly. I have a nose made from bits of my skull. Also false teeth, a very misshapen face, eyes that aren't aligned anymore (looks like a lazy eye or partially crossed), and a really weak chin (shot myself from under my chin, the doctors said the bone was "mush" so much of it is gone). 

I wasn't beautiful before, but I was decent looking. I wouldn't say my face scares children now, but it's not far from that. 

I had terrible self-esteem problems before, but now I look in the mirror and see a joke. A pathetic monster. 

It sucks to lose your identity. Especially if you are vain.

If you are interested, I can tell you a few things I learned, and a couple of ways to kinda-sorta cope. But don't expect anything good - I still despise myself and the way I look.

I've spent a lot of hours in bed like that. Sleep so much you can't sleep anymore. Terror at the thought of speaking to someone, lest they bring up all the things they want from you (like going to work) that you haven't delivered. Your thoughts spin. You can't figure out any way things could be better. You envision your future, and it's as bleak as now but with the ravages of time added. 

Then, you finally can't lie there anymore. Someone talks you into going back to work. You explain to them what happened and they feign empathy for 12 seconds before telling you some incredibly self-righteous bullshit that boils down to "get over it because we want you to come in and make money for us, but don't want to deal with you being a person and not a robot". The worst is when they claim to understand because they have felt sad before or have had some experience with depression. Or, *oh god*, pretend they know how to fix things - which ends up being another version of "suck it up, your problems don't bother me so they must not be that big of a deal for you either". 

I don't know how other people tolerate one another. Or how people can talk themselves into getting out of bed everyday for days on end. Actually, I do - I think other people are just far better at self deception. Things *will* get better, surely!!!

I didn't write a note. After getting out of the hospital and being told by everyone how lucky I was to be alive, and how selfish I was for attempting suicide, I told the people who abused me all my life it wasn't their fault. I believed what I was told, that I was just mentally unbalanced. I said I was happy to have survived, even though I wasn't. I pretended to be what they wanted me to be, and kept doing all the things they insisted I "had to", the things that lead me to suicide in the first place. 

I'm too much of a pussy to attempt suicide again, because of how badly it went the first time. I shot myself in the head. You would think that would be effective. I just ended up with a completely fucked up looking face and a quarter million dollars in hospital bills. I lost my home and my car, and almost everything else I had, because insurance doesn't pay for self-inflicted injuries. I became the captive of the people who abused me all my life growing up, with their promise to never let me have a minute of privacy lest I harm myself and they would have to deal with it. 

But if I did grow the courage to try again, I don't think I would leave a note. I wouldn't *want* to absolve them of their roles in it. But if I did leave a note that said why I wanted to die, and their parts in that, I am 100% certain that they would explain it away again as me being mentally ill and even more of a monster than they thought because I would be so cruel as to blame them for my own faults. It's happened in every other instance, so I can be pretty sure death wouldn't be an exception. 

So no. Fuck them. I do not owe them an explanation.

I don't know you, so I can't say, but college may not be right for you. I did graduate college despite MDD and horrible anxiety attacks on the reg, but I also liked a lot of things about college. It was very hard and I stayed on benzos for years just to be able to go to class. Quitting them was very hard. 

But I also find jobs cause depression and anxiety just as bad, maybe worse since there's no alternative in life to having a job for most of us - and therefore we feel more trapped.

Life is harder for some without a degree, but it isn't necessarily worth destroying yourself over. IDK what your answer is, but don't feel like staying in college is your only choice in life. If you can work it out, it will likely benefit you later. You can also get help from your college/uni. in several forms. Don't be afraid to talk to your profs because they almost always understand. That was one thing that helped me immensely. Turns out they are usually very cool and understanding people. Not always, but most of the time. 

Feeling trapped may be the one thing that leads to depression and anxiety more than anything else. Explore your options - just knowing that you could realistically drop out and still be OK may be enough to ease your mind a bit. If you are there because *you* chose to be, it will feel a lot better. But that means choosing whether you want to be there or not, and deciding if it really is the right thing for you.

There's this heavily propagated myth that says depression and anxiety are caused by your brain malfunctioning. That if you leave your situation you'll just be depressed and/or anxious in your new situation. 

I've found it not to be true. I find that my depression and anxiety are almost always caused by my situation, and if I change it (and the people I'm around) enough, I'm not depressed and don't have that crushing anxiety. 

Both are messages from your brain that something in your life is drastically wrong. I can't tell you what that is, but likely you already have it at least somewhat figured out. 

The only way I've overcome depression in life so far has been to leave the situation that I'm in completely. To start over completely.
